name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos (Jerónimos Monastery)
tagline: Free church with Vasco da Gama's tomb, paid cloister on timed slots; closed on Mondays

description.short: A masterpiece of Portuguese Manueline architecture, this 16th-century monastery stands as Portugal's most visited heritage complex. UNESCO-listed since 1983, it celebrates the Age of Discoveries and houses the tombs of Vasco da Gama and poet Luís de Camões.
description.full:
For a cruise passenger, the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos is usually the first stop in Belém and the one that needs the most planning. The complex has two parts with separate entrances. The church (Igreja de Santa Maria de Belém) is free and holds the tombs of Vasco da Gama and the poet Luís de Camões; it opens to visitors Tuesday to Saturday from 10:30, but only from 14:00 on Sundays because of services. The two-storey cloister is the paid part (€18) and is what most people remember: the carved Manueline arcades are best seen from the upper gallery.

Cloister tickets are sold in hourly timed slots from 09:30, the ticket offices close at 16:30, and the monastery caps visits at 3,500 people a day. Crowds build from mid-morning, so book a slot online before you leave the ship or aim for an early one. Between 09:30 and 10:30 a separate lane is reserved for guided groups. The whole complex is closed on Mondays, which catches out many Monday port calls; the Padrão dos Descobrimentos, MAAT and Pastéis de Belém stay open that day.

If time is short, see the church (20–30 minutes) and the carved south portal from the pavement, then decide whether the cloister justifies €18 on your schedule. With 45 minutes more, do the cloister. The rest of Belém chains together on foot: Pastéis de Belém is about 230 m east along Rua de Belém (3 minutes), the Padrão dos Descobrimentos is roughly 600 m away through the underpass by the Praça do Império garden (about 9 minutes), and the Torre de Belém is about 1.2 km west (around 17 minutes). Belém railway station is roughly 12 minutes' walk.

Begun around 1501 under King Manuel I, the monastery is a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with the tower. Large bags and backpacks are refused at the entrance, and food and drink are not allowed inside.
description.history: The monastery replaced a small riverside chapel where Vasco da Gama and his crew kept vigil before sailing for India on 7 July 1497. Manuel I gave the site to the Order of Saint Jerome, and the foundation stone was laid on 6 January, the Feast of the Epiphany, in 1501 or 1502. Diogo de Boytac was the first master builder; João de Castilho took over in 1517 after finishing the south portal, and the French sculptor Nicolau Chanterene carved the west portal with portraits of Manuel I and Queen Maria. When religious orders were abolished in 1834, the cloister was secularised while the church kept its religious role, which is why the two are still ticketed and timed differently today.
description.significance: Jerónimos is the most visited heritage complex in Portugal and the clearest example of the Manueline style: a late Gothic structure covered in ropes, armillary spheres, sea creatures and royal emblems that advertised the wealth of the sea route to India. The church also works as a national pantheon, with Vasco da Gama and Luís de Camões, author of Os Lusíadas, buried near the entrance. Seeing it first gives context to the tower and the Padrão across the road.

directions.general: Located in the historic Belém district on the Tagus River waterfront, directly facing the Praça do Império gardens
directions.fromCruisePort: About 7.5 km west of the terminal (a 1h40 walk, not practical). Taxi or app car takes 15-20 minutes; alternatively walk to Praça do Comércio and ride tram 15E to the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos stop (about 30-40 minutes), or take the train from Cais do Sodré to Belém.
directions.publicTransport: Tram 15E from Praça do Comércio to Mosteiro Jerónimos stop (30 min). Buses 727, 28, 729, 714, 751 to Mosteiro Jerónimos. Train to Belém station then 5-minute walk.
directions.parking: Public parking available at Praça do Império and Centro Cultural de Belém. Limited street parking nearby.

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open Tuesday to Sunday; closed on Mondays and five public holidays

admissionPrices.comboTicket: No combined Jerónimos + Torre de Belém ticket is listed by the official ticket office; buy two timed tickets (€18 + €15).
admissionPrices.notes: Cloister €18 (official MMP price, unchanged in 2026). Church free. 50% off for visitors aged 65+ and 13–24 with ID (€9); under 12 free with an adult; 50% family discount (at least one adult and one minor). Residents of Portugal can enter free on up to 52 days a year (Acesso 52). Timed hourly slots; ticket offices close 16:30.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: Church 20–30 minutes; church and cloister 1–1.5 hours
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: The first slot at 09:30 or the last slots after 15:30. Remember the church only opens at 10:30 (14:00 on Sundays).
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Book a timed cloister slot online in advance. The church is free and has its own entrance and hours. Large bags, food and drink are not allowed inside. Combine with Pastéis de Belém (3 minutes' walk), the Padrão dos Descobrimentos (via the underpass) and the Torre de Belém (about 17 minutes' walk).

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 3–3.5 hours return from the ship for church and cloister; add 1 hour to include Pastéis de Belém and the Padrão dos Descobrimentos
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Church and lower cloister are on ground level; the upper cloister is stairs only (no wheelchairs or pushchairs). Reach Belém by taxi, tram 15E or train.
tips: Closed on Mondays (church and cloister). On a Monday call, switch to the Padrão dos Descobrimentos, MAAT and Pastéis de Belém, which are open.
Book a timed cloister slot online before you leave the ship: slots run hourly from 09:30 and the ticket offices close at 16:30.
The church is free but opens to visitors only at 10:30 Tuesday–Saturday and at 14:00 on Sundays, so a Sunday-morning visit gets the cloister only.
The ticket kiosk in front of the monastery also sells Torre de Belém tickets; if you have not booked, buy both there before walking to the tower.
Visitors aged 65+ and 13–24 pay half price (€9) with ID; under-12s go free with an adult.
Leave large backpacks on the ship: large bags are refused at the entrance, and food and drink are not allowed inside.
The upper cloister is reached by stairs only; wheelchairs and pushchairs are limited to the church and the lower cloister.
Tram 15E stops outside at Mosteiro Jerónimos; entry is included in the Lisboa Card, which also covers the tram.

highlights: Two-storey Manueline cloister, best viewed from the upper gallery (paid)
Church of Santa Maria de Belém with slender carved columns (free entry)
Tombs of Vasco da Gama and Luís de Camões near the church entrance
South portal facing the river, by João de Castilho
West portal by Nicolau Chanterene with portraits of Manuel I and Queen Maria
Former monks' refectory lined with azulejo tile panels
High chapel in Estremoz marble, added in 1557–1562 by Queen Catherine
facilities: Ticket office with advance booking option
Gift shop with books and souvenirs

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Church and lower cloister are on ground level. Monument rules bar wheelchairs, pushchairs and other mobility devices from the upper floor of the cloister. Call ahead (+351 213 620 034) for assistance.
